cards.explanation: The answer is that he must be put to death. The LORD says, “…who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:2) This is a heavy one, friends, so I'm not going to joke about it. The words are plain, and I'll leave them plain.

The answer is False. The verse names both groups: “Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel…” (Leviticus 20:2) It's a short little phrase, and it's easy to read right over it. Foreigners living in Israel are included in this law along with the Israelites.

The answer is the people of the land. The LORD says, “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) The verse gives this job to the people of the land and names no one else for it. It's a heavy line, so I'll keep to what the verse says.

The answer is that it defiles His sanctuary and profanes His holy name. The LORD gives His reason in His own words: “…he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) The reason is right there in the verse, so we don't have to guess at one. Giving his offspring to Molech touched the LORD's sanctuary and His holy name.

The answer is “family.” The LORD says, “…then I will set My face against that man and his family…” (Leviticus 20:5) So it reaches past the one man to his family too. Verse 5 says this is what follows if the people hide their eyes and don't put the man to death. It's a serious line.

The answer is holy, friends! The LORD says, “Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.” (Leviticus 20:7) All those heavy warnings come before it, and then He says what He wants for His people. I think it lands like a hand on the shoulder after a hard talk. And the reason He gives is who He is, not a list of rules.

The answer is True! The LORD says, “And you shall keep My statutes and practice them.” (Leviticus 20:8) Notice there are two things here. They keep His statutes, and they practice them. He wants them to do something with them, friends.

The answer is the LORD who sanctifies you. The LORD says, “I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” (Leviticus 20:8) To sanctify is to make holy. Just before this, He told them to consecrate themselves and be holy, and here He says He is the One who makes them holy. So they keep His statutes, and He is the One doing the sanctifying.

The answer is his father or mother. The verse says, “If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:9) The LORD names the sin, cursing, and the ones it's aimed at, his father or mother. It's a heavy line, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is that the land won't vomit them out, and it's a colorful wording, friends. The LORD says, “…so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.” (Leviticus 20:22) The land is the one doing the vomiting here. That's the picture the LORD uses, and it's a vivid one to remember.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “You must not follow the statutes of the nations I am driving out before you.” (Leviticus 20:23) Israel isn't free to follow them. Those words are plain, so there's nothing left to guess at.

The answer is that they did all these things. The LORD gives this reason: “Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.” (Leviticus 20:23) The reason is what the nations did. It's a strong word, abhorred, and the LORD picked it Himself.

The answer is True! The LORD says, “But I have told you that you will inherit their land, since I will give it to you as an inheritance…” (Leviticus 20:24) He gives them the land, and He tells them ahead of time. It's good news, friends, right in the middle of a sermon full of serious warnings.

The answer is flowing with milk and honey, bakers! The LORD calls it “…a land flowing with milk and honey.” (Leviticus 20:24) Picture that for a second. It's so full of good things that it's overflowing, like dough rising right over the edge of the bowl. And He says He will give it to them as an inheritance.

The answer is that He set them apart. The LORD says, “I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.” (Leviticus 20:24) Set apart is the wording the LORD uses for what He did with Israel. And it keeps coming back through this whole sermon.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I have set these apart as unclean for you.” (Leviticus 20:25) Right before that, He tells them to distinguish between clean and unclean animals and birds, and not to become contaminated. So the line between them is His, and Israel is told to keep it in view.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “You are to be holy to Me because I, the LORD, am holy…” (Leviticus 20:26) His reason is that He is holy. The nations watching isn't mentioned, and I'd rather hold to what He actually says.
The answer is “own.” The LORD says, “…and I have set you apart from the nations to be My own.” (Leviticus 20:26) It's a short word, and it says a lot. Israel is set apart to belong to Him.

The answer is stoned. The LORD says, “A man or a woman who is a medium or spiritist must surely be put to death. They shall be stoned; their blood is upon them.” (Leviticus 20:27) This is a heavy line, so I'll leave it plain. The LORD names the penalty for both a man and a woman.
